newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money down in early trade, seen easy.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money down in early trade, seen easy.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 5.5-5.85 percent range in early Tuesday trade, down from Monday's closing quotes of 6.25-6.5 percent on improved sentiment, dealers said.
They said sentiment had improved as market participants expected good inflows into banks over the next two weeks.
A debt market report by ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said the net inflow into the banking system between May 21 and May 31 will be in excess of 23 billion rupees.
I-Sec said it expected call money to trade in a range of 3.0 percent to 7.0 percent for the rest of May.

"I think market players realised that the current liquidity levels did not warrant interest rates of 7.0-8.0 percent," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The fall in rates was overdue and people have started quoting lower."
Dealers said the lower call money rates would trigger buying interest in government securities and push prices up.
